content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Erika Bolton (E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes in team memory with conflicting facts:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Admin requires owning role (Payroll Specialist); as Analyst, max is write.
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB shows contractor with basic training. Contractors max read without advanced training; never admin.

Conflict: full_time vs contractor. Security DB note appears more authoritative (it says note conflict with prior note's full-time claim). Security DB is typically authoritative for employment type.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns Payroll). So max write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. This contractor has basic training, so max read.

Either way, admin is above the max. So grant the maximum.

Which max? If full-time: write. If contractor with basic: read. The security note says contractor with basic training → max read.

The conflict is between two notes. The Security DB note explicitly addresses the conflict and claims to be the security DB, which is presumably authoritative. So the employee is a contractor with basic training. Max = read.

Requested admin > max read → grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.

Evidence: conflicting notes; Security DB shows contractor with basic security training; contractors max read without advanced training; never admin; requested admin exceeds max, grant max = read.
